name: Diogo Cão to the Congo and Namibia
summary: On two voyages Diogo Cão pushes the known coast of Africa twenty degrees further south. At the mouth of a great river he raises a stone pillar, a padrão, and learns of the kingdom of Kongo inland; he carves his name on the rocks at the Yellala falls upriver. On the second voyage he reaches Cape Cross on the coast of Namibia, sets up his last pillar, and vanishes from the record.

stops.note: The first voyage sails with stone pillars carved with the arms of Portugal.
The new castle on the Gold Coast.
A river so strong it freshens the sea far offshore; the first padrão, at Shark Point.
The second padrão, on the coast of Angola.
He brings back Kongo men to learn Portuguese.
Back with the envoys to the king of Kongo.
Up the river to the rapids, where his men carve their names on a rock.
The last padrão, on the desert coast of Namibia; after this Cão disappears.
